title: Load an ASTM D638 dogbone into two spring-closed wedge grips, jogging the test stand crosshead onto it
instruction: Load the dogbone specimen into both wedge grips of the tensile test stand at the 115 mm test length, straight and flat, then step away from the stand.
context: Tensile testing of moulded or 3D-printed plastic specimens (ASTM D638 Type I, 165 mm long, 115 mm between the grips) is the basic measurement behind polymer and materials-research studies, and loading the specimen into the grips is the first step of every tensile test. A self-driving materials lab can only automate those studies if a robot can do this step: one grip is spring-closed and opens only 6.4 mm, so a lever is held open while the 3.2 mm-thick tab is slid in, then the stand's jog key is held to move the second grip onto the other tab and both are clamped straight. A specimen gripped at an angle, off the jaw centre or pushed against a slot end tears early and the result is discarded.
setup: Station table top 0.7475 m; origin midway between the arm bases, x forward, y left, metres. Green ESD bench mat 420 x 600 x 3 mm at (0.27, 0). Horizontal motorized force test stand (grey base 130 x 460 x 40 mm) along y at (0.30, 0), loading axis 76 mm above the mat: force indicator with its load cell and grip A fixed at the +y end; grip B on the motorised crosshead at the -y end, backed off 35 mm at the start (jaw faces 150 mm apart, as left after a test). Two wedge grips at the maker's drawing size: black housing 38.1 (x) x 62.2 (y) x 49.5 (z) mm, serrated jaws 19.1 mm wide, jaw gap 0-6.4 mm (horizontal jaws), thru slot open at the front and back (x), slot ends 33 mm behind the jaw faces; the slot floor's front edge has a 3 mm 45 deg lead-in. Each upper jaw is spring-closed onto the lower jaw or a tab. Its red lever handle (6 x 26 x 30 mm, top 0.135 m above the table) sits behind the housing at x 0.326 (grip A y +0.074; grip B y -0.109 at the start, moving with the crosshead); pushed 22 mm back (+x) against its return spring (6.6 N) it lifts the jaw to a 6.2 mm gap; let go, the spring returns it and the jaw spring clamps the tab with 1.9 N. Jog box at the +y end of the frame, keys up, 24 mm square, tops 0.089 m above the mat at y 0.285: LEFT (x 0.255), STOP, RIGHT (x 0.345). While LEFT is held down the crosshead moves +y at 500 mm/min, while RIGHT is held it moves back (momentary keys), release stops it; 115.0 mm jaw-face distance is 35 mm of LEFT travel, the stop 15 mm further. Both grips start closed. Loose: one ASTM D638 Type I dogbone (165 x 19 x 3.2 mm, 13 x 57 mm neck, 7.8 g) carrying a pen mark 17 mm from each tab end lying flat along y on a blue specimen tray at (0.18, 0) with two 4 mm back stops at x 0.2005, underside 12 mm above the table. Behind the stand, visual only (out of reach): a PC keyboard, a mouse on its pad, a vernier caliper and safety glasses.
scoring: Scored at the last step from the end state alone; every row is a ruler, protractor or photo check. How to check by hand: a pen mark 17 mm from each tab end is hidden behind its jaw face once the tab is in that deep (photo); the slot is open at the front, so the 2 mm end gap is seen from the side and checked with a 2 mm feeler; 2 deg over the 115 mm between the jaws is a 4 mm offset (ruler or protractor). Seated = the tab is inside the slot between the jaws, past the 17 mm ruler mark at its jaw face (not beyond the slot end) and overhangs its jaw by at most 4 mm. Each grip's rows count on their own (the -y tab needs nothing from the +y tab): +0.10 +y tab seated; +0.10 lever A fully forward (within 2 mm of its forward stop: let go) and the jaw closed on the tab (jaw gap at most 4.7 mm, 1.5 mm over the 3.2 mm tab: no feeler thicker than 1.5 mm fits between the jaw and the tab) with the +y tab seated; +0.05 the seated +y tab's end leaves a 2 mm gap to its slot end; +0.10, +0.10, +0.05 the same three rows for the -y tab, lever B and its jaw. Once both tabs are clamped (seated, levers forward and each jaw gap at most 4.7 mm): +0.15 specimen within 2 deg of the pull axis in yaw and pitch (protractor); +0.20 jaw faces 115 +- 5 mm apart (ruler; ASTM D638 distance between grips); +0.15 both grippers at least 5 cm from the specimen, both levers and both jog keys (photo). Success = full score held 3 s (the trial then ends; the hold adds no score). Possible scores 0, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.45, 0.5, 0.55, 0.6, 0.65, 0.7, 0.75, 0.8, 0.85, 0.95, 1. 0: no tab seated (not placed, on top of a jaw, off the jaw, knocked off), even with the crosshead jogged to 115 mm.
run_limit: 900 steps (45 s at 20 Hz); the demo takes about 580 steps
reset_notes: Put the dogbone back flat on its tray against the back stops, redraw the pen mark 17 mm from each tab end, jog the crosshead back 35 mm (jaw faces 150 mm apart, ruler between the jaw faces) and leave both levers forward. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Grips at drawing size (19.1 mm jaws, 0-6.4 mm opening, thru slot). Scene layout (460 mm frame, 76 mm axis, indicator) follows a commercial stand; the real stage has 200 mm travel, no indicator. Lever: 22 mm spring-return slide lifting the jaw to 6.2 mm. Ends at mounting, no pull: the 1.9 N jaw spring holds the tab; wedge self-tightening not modelled. Crosshead: servo at 500 mm/min while a jog key is held. Real stage: horizontal rating 30 kg: mounting, clamp, jog, not a 500 N pull.
